Subject: Sierra Tech Dedicated: warm-pool, burst fallback & autoscale runbook

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the call today. As we discussed, we want to lock in a Dedicated capacity plan that gives Sierra Tech predictable steady-state throughput while handling periodic model-driven spikes during reporting windows. Attached is a first-pass proposal (sierra-dedicated-proposal-v1.pdf) — key points below: 

- Baseline slab: 16x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved for your steady traffic.
- Warm pool: +4 GPU warm nodes (prewarmed, lower cost) to shorten scale-up on spike.
- Burst credit bucket: 200 GPU-minutes/month that can be consumed for short high-throughput windows.
- Autoscale policy: conservative scale-up trigger, immediate prewarm, and graceful scale-down window.

Questions for your procurement/ops team:
1) Typical peak window length and expected peak QPS during report runs?
2) Any regulatory requirement that would forbid prewarming on shared hosts (we can provide isolated warm nodes if needed).

Next step: would love to schedule a short technical session this week with Ben and Karthik from our infra team to align on concrete thresholds and eviction rules. Are you available Thu 23rd or Fri morning?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett

Hi Laura —

Thanks for sending this over. High level this looks good. A few clarifying points from our side before the tech call: 

- Peak windows: usually 6–12 minutes, 2–3 times per day during ET end-of-day reporting; occasional longer runs (30–45m) around fiscal month-end.
- Throughput: peak token rate roughly 3–4x baseline; some bursts are latency-sensitive (sub-200ms tails for small chat workloads).
- Compliance: we prefer warm nodes to be tenant-dedicated for audit reasons; shared prewarm is okay only for stateless inferencing.

Can Ben and Karthik propose concrete autoscale thresholds and eviction rules? We also need a brief note on how SLA/credits behave when burst credits are consumed. Thu 23rd at 10am PT works for me.

— Sarah

Hi Sarah / Laura —

Quick technical proposal ahead of Thu's call so we have a baseline to iterate on. Summary (high level) followed by specifics: 

Summary recommendations:
- Scale-up trigger: when aggregate GPU utilization across the dedicated slab + warm pool crosses 65% for a sustained 90s window.
- Prewarm window: spin warm node to hot node in ~90–180s; keep warm pool at +4 by default.
- Burst bucket: 200 GPU-minutes/month (as proposed) with rollover disabled; auto-fallback to quantized lower-cost model variant when bucket depleted.
- Eviction policy: preemptible jobs are evicted first; critical low-latency jobs pinned to tenant-dedicated nodes won't be evicted.

More detail (operational knobs):
- Headroom sizing guidance:
  * Baseline slab: 16 GPUs (reserved).
  * Warm pool: 4 GPUs (prewarmed, tenant-dedicated as requested).
  * Hot-standby: 2 spare GPUs in the same region for emergency scale beyond warm pool.

- Autoscale thresholds (initial):
  * scale-up (add 2 GPUs): aggregate utilization >= 65% for 90s or 80% for 30s.
  * scale-up (add 4 GPUs): aggregate utilization >= 80% for 120s.
  * scale-down: utilization <= 40% for 10 minutes (graceful drain with 60s per-connection soft stop).

- Preemption & eviction rules:
  * Order: opportunistic batch > best-effort workers > interactive chat (pinned).
  * When burst credits exhausted, traffic to heavy endpoints routes to quantized-model endpoint (same API surface, -2–3% quality delta in our benchmarks).

- Monitoring & telemetry hooks:
  * Per-GPU utilization + queue depth metric exported to Sierra Tech's PagerDuty channel.
  * Token-level cost meter for every route (for visibility during bursts).

Attachments included: burst_matrix_v2.xlsx (headroom scenarios & cost simulation) and autoscale_policy_draft.md (policies in markdown). We'll walk through these on Thu and lock conservative defaults; can tune after two weeks in production based on observed spike shapes.

Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
